## Question 1: What was the capability BEFORE the PAM-SI (2023)?

***Drop-down selections:*** Proof of Concept, Pilot Study, Potentially
Operational, Operational, Not Applicable

This question relates to this specific COMPONENT of the workflow.

- ***Proof of Concept:*** a small scale demonstration showing
  feasability

- ***Pilot Study:*** study in real-world conditions

- ***Potentially Operational:*** successful implementation of pilot
  study, or implementation in other related studies. Shows potential for
  operationalization but not yet operational.

- ***Operational:*** used operationally

- ***Not Applicable:*** no capabilities

***Why?*** We want to reflect on the impact the PAM Strategic Initiative
had on the improvement of different components of our workflow and
across the different science centers.

## Question 2: What is the current capability?

***Drop-down selections:*** Proof of Concept, Pilot Study, Potentially
Operational, Operational, Not Applicable

This question relates to this specific COMPONENT of the workflow (see
descriptions from Q1).

***Why?*** We want to understand the current capabilities of components
of our workflow and across the different science centers. This will help
us prioritize investment.

## Question 3: What was the level for Automation BEFORE the PAM-SI?

***Drop-down selections:*** Low, Medium, High, Unknown, Not Applicable

This question relates to this specific COMPONENT of the workflow:

- ***Low:*** Little or no automation (largely manual effort)

- ***Medium:*** Moderate level of automation but with one or more areas
  requiring significant manual effort)

- ***High:*** Significant levels of automation with low levels of manual
  effort required

- ***Unknown:*** Only use this if it is truly unknown

- ***Not Applicable:*** There is little/no potential for automation of
  this workflow component.

***Why?*** We want to reflect on the impact the PAM Strategic Initiative
had on the improvement of different components of our workflow and
across the different science centers.

## Question 6: How painful is the current process?

***Drop-down selections:*** All Good, Room for Improvement, Painful!,
Blocked

This question relates to this specific COMPONENT of the workflow:

- ***All Good:*** This workflow component is highly functional and
  requires little more than minor improvements

- ***Room for Improvement:*** This workflow component functions, but
  there is still significant room for improvement

- ***Painful!:*** This process functions but has significant 'pain
  points' (large or small) that lead to high (or unneccesary) levels of
  frustration

- ***Blocked:*** This workflow component is important/needed but either
  does not exist or is not functional

***Why?*** Understanding pain points helps us identify critical
components of our workflow that are negatively impacting not only our
success and efficiency, but also our morale. For example, some process
may appear to be efficient (highly automated), but there may be
frustrating small barriers that have an out-sized impact. This will help
us prioritize future investment.

## Question 9: What was the operating model BEFORE the PAM-SI (2023)?

***Drop-down selections:*** Center-Run, Regional Hub,
National/Centralized, Outsourced

This question relates to this specific COMPONENT of the workflow. An
'Operating Model' is how this component is developed & maintained. Many
workflow components require a combination of efforts. Users can select
more than one operating model, if appropriate.

- ***National/Centralized:*** a centralized body develops and maintains
  this workflow component.

- ***Regional Hub:*** Development, assets, and technical staff are
  shared to support shared regional missions.

- ***Center-run:*** Niche components or thos with a deep expertise
  legacy may be developed, maintained, and implemented at a local
  center-run level.

- ***Outsourced:*** NMFS focuses on needs/specifications and outsources
  the work attributed to this workflow component.

***Why?*** We want to reflect on the impact the PAM Strategic Initiative
had on the improvement of different components of our workflow and
across the different science centers.

## Question 10: What is the current operating model?

***Drop-down selections:*** Center-Run, Regional Hub,
National/Centralized, Outsourced

This question relates to this specific COMPONENT of the workflow (see
descriptions from Q9).

***Why?*** We'd like to understand the current operating model,
especially as it relates to the operating model used before the PAM-SI
and as it relates to the ideal operating model.

## Question 11: What is the ideal operating model?

***Drop-down selections:*** Center-Run, Regional Hub,
National/Centralized, Outsourced

This question relates to this specific COMPONENT of the workflow (see
descriptions from Q9).

***Why?*** By understanding the user-defined 'ideal' operating model,
this can help us areas where we need to expend effort to centralize
effort for a more national strategy.

## Question 12: What is needed achieve an ideal operating model? (Text)

Describe potential modifications to the way we work that you think would
help us achieve an ideal operational model.

***Why?*** We understand that each team will have a different idea for
ways we can work together (nationally and/or regionally) as well as ways
in which teams prefer to operate independently. These answers will help
teams think about what they think is an ideal way to work, which will
help us identify the ways in which we need to come together.
